An unusual sight was that of a Belgrave senior team winning the 4 x 110y but of course our quartet were all first year seniors, fresh out of the junior ranks where Belgrave sprinters are amongst the…
Most of our points were scored by decathlon man Barry Townsend with a 2nd in the 110m Hurdles, 3rd in the Pole Vault and 6th in the High Jump.
In the Long Jump, John Mitchell was forced to take 2nd place behind Kelly (HHH) with Bob Couillaut 4th and Barry Townsend 6th, only 1'7" covering the first six competitors.

In the Javelin, Brian King threw over 9'0" further than before to beat Colin Clair by only 1" with Barry Townsend 3rd. Brian's magnificent effort just halted Colin's bid for a treble as he took the discus and shot, both with best distances by Belgravians so far this year.

Barry Townsend was in top form and set up personal bests in the Pole Vault(2nd with 11'4") and High Jump(3rd with 5'11"). His potential decathlon score is now quite impressive as he has already reached a 16.5/110mH, 20'10"/LJ, 155'11"/Jav, 33'5"/Shot and 99'8"Discus - all this year.
In winning the High Jump with a personal best of 6'0", Barry Townsend became the first Belgravian to clear this height since Mal Ash in 1958 .

Four men cleared 5'9" in the High Jump but Barry Townsend was placed 6th on the count-back of failures. The Long Jump also produced a close finish with Howell (HHH) winning with 22'8" and Bob Jones and Hudson (TVH) both reaching 22'3½".
Barry Townsend was with him over the first five flights but lost ground towards the finish. Another who was well up, until a near fall almost put him out of the race, was Bob Jones.
The Triple Jump saw a rare defeat for Bob Couillaut by fellow club man Barry Townsend who cleared his previous best by over a foot. There were no fewer than six Bels. competing in this event.
17th/18th September - Charlton Park - KENT DECATHLON CHAMP. 1.A.Lattimer (Herne Hill H) 5551 pts 2.J.Wright (Blackheath) 5524 pts 3.B.Townsend (BELGRAVE H) 5403 pts
Senior Club Records were set by John Thresher (2m), Barry Townsend (Decathlon) Malcolm Robinson (3m), Geoff North (3m), John Bicourt (3000mSC) and equalled by Colin Clair (Jav).
Barry Townsend has already had a go at 6 feet in the High Jump (unsuccessfully) and is certain to improve when he becomes fitter. Denzil Winsborrow has been Vaulting and jumping extremely well.

The conditions sadly affected our field event men with Nick Head being injured in the Javelin, our two Long Jumpers suffering from the anti-climax of their performances the previous week and Barry Townsend recovering from the SCAAA Decathlon held the day before.
Barry Townsend was kept busy taking 3rd in the 'A' Long Jump, 2nd in the 'A' High Jump and 2nd in thr 'B' Javelin with a good throw of 158'8½ to beat an off-form Brian King in the 'A' event.

Denzil Winsborrow and Barry Townsend filled 2nd and 4th places in the Pole Vault and also scored heavily in the High Jump. Top points scorer of the day, though, was Nicholas Head with 3rd in the Javelin and 5th in the Shot and Discus, both the latter being close to his best ever.

Derek Wade made 2nd in the Long Jump, Denzil Winsborrow vaulted into 4th place despite a treacherous wind that removed the bar without any help from the competitors, and Barry Townsend recorded his best marks of the season with a 16.5 High Hurdles effort and a 5'11" High Jump.
Our pole vaulters Barry Townsend and Denzil Winsborrow will certainly master the fibre glass pole and then (not wanting to be corny) "the sky's the limit".
